moat_source: brand and global distribution system without peer; evidence: +10% organic growth with 35% operating margins and pricing power straight through a GLP-1 demand shock

returns.assumption_note: Convergence to scenario IV by year 5, ~60% closed by year 3. Excludes the ~2.4% covered dividend, which offsets roughly a quarter of the expected decline. Net debt (~$25B, order-of-magnitude from public balance-sheet convention, not freshly sourced) netted from equity values.

sensitivity_key_driver: the discount-rate regime (framework artifact - see primary model risk)
primary_model_risk: Hurdle-rate mismatch, disclosed openly: KO's cash flows are among the most predictable on Earth, and the market prices them at a ~6-7% required return (beta 0.35). This framework pins 10% for cross-name comparability, which mechanically renders every low-beta defensive 'overvalued.' The avoid verdict means 'KO cannot clear a 10% return hurdle from $83.78' - a true statement - not 'KO is a broken business.' At an 8% discount rate the base case would roughly double.
expectations_gap_key_variable: required return: the market and this framework agree on KO's cash flows and disagree only on the discount rate; within the framework's 10% constraint the stock cannot offer an adequate expected return from this price
top_5_bull_arguments: Best-in-class execution: +10% organic, +18% EPS, margin expansion, raised guidance - the strongest operating print among all staples analyzed
The dividend is COVERED (~72% of guided $12.2B FCF) - the exact test PEP failed
Coke Zero +13% volumes shows the portfolio is navigating GLP-1 rather than denying it
64 consecutive dividend increases with a $5.2B buyback on top
Beta 0.35 - genuine ballast against the AI-concentrated remainder of this list
top_5_bear_arguments: ~30x FCF for mid-single-digit terminal growth cannot clear a 10% hurdle under any scenario modeled - even the bull case ($68.30) sits below the price
GLP-1 usage inflects upward in 2026 (patent expiries, oral forms) - the exposed full-sugar base erodes structurally
Organic growth of 10% is above KO's own trend and will normalize toward 4-6%, compressing the premium multiple
~$25B net debt narrows flexibility versus its history
Defensive scarcity premium evaporates if rates fall and growth rotates back
thesis_breakers: Organic revenue growth below 4% for two consecutive quarters
FCF guidance cut below $11B (dividend coverage narrowing)
Global unit-case volume declining y/y (GLP-1 winning)
Dividend growth pause (unthinkable until it happens)
position_size_recommendation: 0% under this framework's hurdle; investors running a lower required return for defensive ballast may reasonably disagree - that disagreement is the entire question, and it is disclosed rather than smoothed over
notes_on_nulls: ROIC/ROE/ROA null: not captured as sourced ratios. Revenue/EPS/guidance/FCF-guide reported (press release); net debt is an order-of-magnitude convention figure, flagged. The verdict is hurdle-rate-driven (see primary_model_risk) - the lowest probability_of_permanent_loss (8%) on any name analyzed coexists with an avoid, which is the framework working as designed, not a contradiction.
